references.text: Describes the same measurements for the grain offering: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of oil, and a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering accompanying the burnt offering.
Specifies a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of oil as the grain offering for the daily burnt offering.
Mentions the drink offering of wine that must accompany the burnt offering: a quarter hin for each lamb.
Basic instruction regarding the grain offering of fine flour with oil, which forms the basis for the sacrificial practice described here.
Describes the grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil together with a drink offering of wine.
Mentions pure, pressed olive oil (shemen katit) that is also used in this grain offering.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple includes similar grain offerings of fine flour and oil every morning.
Establishes the standard for the daily Tamid offering based on the specifications of the consecration ritual.
Generalizes the specifications of the consecration ritual into a general law for the people of Israel.
Confirms that the drink offering (wine) follows the same standard for all lamb sacrifices.
